articles.title: Auto Horror in Salem: Distracted Driving Turns Quiet Street into Danger Zone #breakingnews
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing video from Salem has gone viral, showing an auto-rickshaw ramming into a pedestrian on a narrow residential street, raising fresh concerns over road safety and driver negligence.

body.html:
A disturbing video from Salem has gone viral, showing an auto-rickshaw ramming into a pedestrian on a narrow residential street, raising fresh concerns over road safety and driver negligence.

As per social media posts, the incident occurred on a stretch with a speed hump meant to slow vehicles. However, the auto driver appeared inattentive and failed to notice the pedestrian ahead, hitting the person before the vehicle toppled over.

Panic gripped the area as local residents rushed to help. The visuals, described as disturbing, drew sharp reactions online, with many questioning reckless driving even on traffic-calmed roads.

Road safety activists have called for stricter monitoring of auto drivers, better training, and tougher action against distracted driving. There is no official update yet on the pedestrian’s condition.

The incident highlights growing concerns over road discipline and pedestrian safety in residential areas.

articles.title: “Married by Choice, Not Abducted”: Amroha Woman’s Viral Video Seeks Police Protection
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A young woman from the Hasanpur police station area in Amroha district has shared a video on social media after her court marriage, claiming she married by choice and is facing threats from her family.

body.html:
A young woman from the Hasanpur police station area in Amroha district has shared a video on social media after her court marriage, claiming she married by choice and is facing threats from her family.

In the viral video, Manisha said she is 18 years old and legally capable of taking her own decisions. She stated that she married Roopchand in court of her own free will and was not abducted. “I came with him willingly,” she said.

The woman alleged that after her family learnt about the love affair, her mother asked her to either die or leave home to save their money. She appealed to the police administration for protection, claiming that her life and that of her husband are in danger from her family members.

Manisha also urged the police not to harass Roopchand’s family, saying they were unaware of their marriage. She warned that if any harm comes to them, her family should be held responsible.

Police are yet to issue an official statement on the matter.

articles.title: Love Affair Turns Deadly: Auto Driver Strangles Wife in Varanasi, Tattoos Expose Killer
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking murder case has surfaced in Varanasi, where 26-year-old Lakshmi was allegedly killed by her husband, Pradeep Mishra (46), an auto driver, following frequent disputes over her alleged love affair. The crime took place on December 19, while her body was recovered on December 21.

body.html:
A shocking murder case has surfaced in Varanasi, where 26-year-old Lakshmi was allegedly killed by her husband, Pradeep Mishra (46), an auto driver, following frequent disputes over her alleged love affair. The crime took place on December 19, while her body was recovered on December 21.

Police said Pradeep confessed that marital discord over the past six months drove him to the act. Lakshmi had reportedly left home thrice with her boyfriend and returned only on December 18. On December 19, Pradeep took her and their children to his sister’s house in Chandwak village and later took Lakshmi out on the pretext of a walk.

Near Kaithor village, he allegedly strangled her with a muffler, smashed her face with bricks to prevent identification, and hid the body in a field. The case appeared blind until tattoos “PL” and “GPL” on Lakshmi’s hands led police to Pradeep, who said they stood for Pradeep-Lakshmi and Guddu-Pradeep-Lakshmi.

Neighbours confirmed frequent fights, and an earlier complaint at Chaubepur police station had ended in counselling. Further probe revealed Pradeep is a history-sheeter with at least seven cases, including a murder, and had spent about 10 years in jail, with his property seized thrice.

Pradeep has been arrested and sent to judicial custody. The couple’s children are currently with relatives and have not yet been informed of the tragedy.

articles.title: Sambhal Blind Murder Cracked: Wife, Lover Arrested After Dismembered Body Found in Drain
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Uttar Pradesh Police have solved a chilling blind murder case in Sambhal district, in which a woman and her lover allegedly killed her husband, dismembered his body, and dumped the parts at different locations to mislead investigators.

body.html:
Uttar Pradesh Police have solved a chilling blind murder case in Sambhal district, in which a woman and her lover allegedly killed her husband, dismembered his body, and dumped the parts at different locations to mislead investigators.

The case came to light on December 15, when Chandausi Kotwali police recovered a severely decomposed torso stuffed in a black bag from behind an Idgah on Patroua Road. The body was missing its head and limbs, making identification difficult.

During forensic examination, police noticed a tattoo with the name “Rahul” on the severed arm, which proved to be a crucial breakthrough. A check of missing person records revealed that a woman named Ruby, a resident of Chunni Mohalla, had filed a complaint on November 24 stating that her husband Rahul had gone missing since November 18.

Ruby was called for questioning, but she denied that the torso belonged to her husband. However, police grew suspicious due to contradictions in her statements and her nervous behaviour. A search of her mobile phone further exposed the truth, as officers found photographs of Rahul wearing the same T-shirt that was recovered with the mutilated body.

Confronted with the evidence, Ruby broke down and confessed that she had been having an affair with a local youth, Gaurav. She told police that on the night of November 17–18, Rahul caught them in a compromising position at home, leading to a heated argument. In a fit of rage, Rahul was allegedly assaulted and killed.

To destroy evidence, Ruby and Gaurav allegedly used a cutter machine to chop the body into pieces. Police said the head and limbs were packed into one bag and thrown into the Ganges near Rajghat, while the torso was dumped near the Idgah on Patroua Road. Ruby later filed a missing report to divert suspicion.

A subsequent search of the house led to the recovery of the cutter machine and other incriminating materials, while forensic teams found signs that the body had been dismembered inside the residence. Neighbours’ statements and inputs from the couple’s 10-year-old daughter also helped investigators piece together the conspiracy.

Both Ruby and Gaurav have been arrested and produced in court. Police are continuing efforts to recover the remaining body parts and strengthen the case with forensic and scientific evidence.

Officials said it was the combination of the tattoo on the decomposed body and the mobile phone photographs that ultimately exposed what was initially believed to be a near-perfect crime. The brutal murder has sent shockwaves across Sambhal.

articles.title: Hyderabad Woman Kills Husband with Lover’s Help, Murder Initially Staged as Heart Attack
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In Medipally police station limits of the Rachakonda Commissionerate, a woman (36) allegedly murdered her husband with the help of her lover and another accomplice, initially attempting to pass it off as a heart attack. The deceased, V.K.

body.html:
In Medipally police station limits of the Rachakonda Commissionerate, a woman (36) allegedly murdered her husband with the help of her lover and another accomplice, initially attempting to pass it off as a heart attack.

The deceased, V.K. Ashok (45), was a resident of Brindavan Colony, Boduppal, and worked at a private college. He lived with his wife Poornima and their son (11). Poornima supplemented the family income by giving tuition to children at home.

Police said Poornima had developed an extramarital relationship with Paleti Mahesh (22), a resident of the same colony. Ashok had reportedly warned her several times after learning about the affair. Believing that her husband was an obstacle to the relationship, Poornima allegedly conspired with Mahesh and his friend Bhukya Sai Kumar (22) to eliminate him.

On the evening of Dec11, around 6:15 PM, when Ashok returned home from work, Mahesh and Sai allegedly caught hold of him while Poornima held his legs. The trio strangled him using a saree and a chain, killing him on the spot. After the murder, they changed the victim’s clothes, removed blood-stained items, and attempted to destroy evidence.

The next day, Poornima lodged a complaint stating that Ashok was found unconscious in the bathroom and had died of a heart attack at the Malkajgiri Government Hospital. Initially, police registered a general case. However, Ashok’s family members raised suspicions against Poornima.

A post-mortem examination revealed that Ashok had been strangled to death, with injuries on his cheek and neck and broken teeth. CCTV footage and technical evidence further strengthened the case. During interrogation, Poornima, Mahesh, and Sai confessed to the crime.

Police arrested all three accused and seized blood-stained chains, clothes, a pen drive containing photos and videos related to the murder, an iPhone-15, and a bike. The case has been altered from Section 194 BNS to Sections 103(1) and 238 read with 3(5) of the BNS, and the accused have been remanded to judicial custody.

Medipally police stated that the case is being strengthened with scientific and forensic evidence as further investigation continues.

articles.title: Help Turned Trap: Bengaluru Woman Alleges Harassment After Taking ₹30,000 Loan from Friend
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Rajagopalnagar Police have registered a case of sexual harassment against a man for allegedly subjecting a 32-year-old married woman to mental and physical harassment after offering her financial help during a crisis.

body.html:
The Rajagopalnagar Police have registered a case of sexual harassment against a man for allegedly subjecting a 32-year-old married woman to mental and physical harassment after offering her financial help during a crisis.

According to the complaint, the woman came in contact with the accused, identified as Paritosh Yadav, through social media, and the two later became friends. During this period, the woman’s daughter suffered serious injuries due to a gas cylinder leak at their residence.

For her daughter’s medical treatment, the woman reportedly borrowed ₹30,000 from Yadav. Police said the accused later used the loan as leverage to harass her and allegedly pressured her into a physical relationship.

The matter eventually came to the notice of the woman’s husband, leading to marital discord. Distressed by the situation, the woman allegedly attempted to end her life at a friend’s house in Peenya. However, timely intervention by her friends saved her.

Subsequently, the woman approached the Rajagopalnagar Police Station and lodged a complaint, seeking action against the accused for mental harassment. Based on her complaint, police have registered a case and said an investigation is underway.

articles.title: Doctor vs Patient Inside Shimla Hospital: Viral Video Sparks Outrage at IGMC
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video showing a physical altercation between a doctor and a patient inside Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC) in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, has surfaced on social media, triggering outrage and calls for action.

body.html:
A video showing a physical altercation between a doctor and a patient inside Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC) in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, has surfaced on social media, triggering outrage and calls for action.

The clip shows the patient lying on a hospital bed and kicking the doctor, while the doctor dodges the blows and punches the patient several times in the face. Others present in the ward are seen intervening to separate the two.

According to reports, the patient has been identified as Arjun Panwar, who had visited IGMC for an endoscopy. After experiencing breathing difficulties, he allegedly went to another ward and lay down on a bed. It is claimed that a doctor later misbehaved with him, leading to a heated argument that soon escalated into a physical fight.

The video went viral, following which the patient’s attendants demanded strict action against the doctor. A police complaint has also been lodged in connection with the incident.

So far, the hospital administration has not issued any official statement. Meanwhile, reports said people gathered outside IGMC as news of the incident spread in Shimla, demanding an inquiry and appropriate action against those responsible.

The viral footage has drawn mixed reactions online, with some users condemning the doctor’s conduct, while others urged restraint until the full facts are known.
